candidates.title: What actually pops when you crack your knuckles?
candidates.opening_promise: That pop isn't your bones. Here's what an MRI saw.

thumbnail.concept: huge fist, burst at the knuckles, 'NOT BONES' rules out the obvious answer

candidates.description: Scientists filmed a knuckle cracking inside an MRI: the joint pulls apart and a gas cavity forms in the fluid.

candidates.title: An MRI filmed a knuckle crack as it happened
candidates.opening_promise: What pops when a knuckle cracks? An MRI caught it happening.

thumbnail.concept: joint cross-section filling the frame, one big bubble in the gap

candidates.description: Inside an MRI, a cracking knuckle shows a gas cavity snapping open in the joint fluid. A 2018 model says the sound may still come from a partial collapse.

candidates.title: Does cracking your knuckles cause arthritis?
candidates.opening_promise: Cracking your knuckles: what actually pops, and is it hurting your joints?

thumbnail.concept: fist with a big question mark; '215 PEOPLE' signals there is real evidence behind the answer

candidates.description: What pops when you crack your knuckles, and what a study of 215 people found about arthritis.

candidates.title: He cracked one hand for 60 years to test it
candidates.opening_promise: One doctor ran a 60-year experiment on his own knuckles.
candidates.description: A doctor cracked only his left hand for 60 years and compared both hands.
